title: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: OpenAI positions GPT-6 Astra as a stronger model for coding, science, cybersecurity, and computer-use workflows, making model admission and tool-permission gates more important than raw capability claims.
actionable_takeaway: Create an Astra Model Admission Checklist before changing any default model: entry point, default state, tool scope, budget, fallback, and rollback.

title: Safety overview: GPT-6 Astra
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: OpenAI describes improved robustness around browsing, workplace tasks, and prompt injection, while also warning that stronger capability raises cyber and monitoring risks.
actionable_takeaway: For computer-use agents, define allowed systems, forbidden actions, monitoring evidence, and human-stop conditions before granting tools.

title: GPT-6 Astra model documentation
author: OpenAI Developers
why_it_matters: The model documentation is the operational reference for API availability, pricing, context, modalities, and endpoint support, which are separate from marketing launch language.
actionable_takeaway: Treat developer docs as the source of truth for API integration; record model key, context, supported endpoints, and pricing in model receipts.

title: Codex 0.153.1 adds API-configurable GPT-6-Astra without changing defaults
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: Codex can configure GPT-6-Astra through the API model catalog, but the release explicitly keeps the default model and model picker unchanged.
actionable_takeaway: Separate model-catalog availability from default activation; keep alpha/model-catalog experiments outside the stable lane until local validation passes.

title: Codex 0.154.0-alpha.3 continues the alpha lane
author: OpenAI / GitHub
why_it_matters: A newer alpha appears after the stable-facing 0.153.1 change, so release cadence is moving faster than stable operating guidance.
actionable_takeaway: Track alpha releases for direction only; require fixed tasks, owner, rollback, and local evidence before promoting any alpha behavior.

title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83-5 gates localhost access in sandbox
author: GitHub / GitHub releases
why_it_matters: The release notes say macOS and Linux sandboxes block access to locally running services by default, requiring explicit Allow local network for localhost testing.
actionable_takeaway: Add a Localhost Sandbox Test Gate to any agent-driven dev-server, Playwright, or E2E task that needs 127.0.0.1 access.

title: Gemini 3.8 Flash is available in GitHub Copilot public preview
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub continues to expand Copilot's model catalog, increasing the need to manage model selection, team defaults, and fallback rules instead of relying on a single provider mental model.
actionable_takeaway: Maintain a team model directory with approved models, allowed surfaces, retention notes, and fallback order.

title: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Copilot model retirement means saved prompts, default settings, and automation receipts can drift even when local code does not change.
actionable_takeaway: Audit automations and team defaults for deprecated model IDs; store replacement model, cutoff date, and rollback plan.

title: Reopening Copilot Business and Enterprise signups
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Credit-card and PayPal signups for Copilot Business and Enterprise reopen, so smaller teams can reach enterprise-style controls without sales-led onboarding.
actionable_takeaway: For team trials, prepare access policy, budget, content exclusions, and default-model settings before enabling paid signup.

title: GitHub Actions early September 2026 updates
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Actions adds runner deprecation APIs, vulnerability-alerts read permission, and reusable workflow metadata in job context, improving CI provenance and least-privilege controls.
actionable_takeaway: Record runner retirement, vulnerability-alert read scope, and reusable workflow provenance in CI release receipts.

title: CodeQL 2.26.4 improves GitHub Actions security detections
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: CodeQL improves detection of mutable reusable workflow references and other Actions hardening issues, which directly affects agent-generated CI changes.
actionable_takeaway: Require sha pinning or documented exceptions for third-party and cross-repository reusable workflows created by agents.

title: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: npm trusted publishing can now support multiple OIDC configurations for the same package, enabling stable, prerelease, and staging lanes without long-lived tokens.
actionable_takeaway: Build a Staged Publishing OIDC Matrix and verify additive matching does not accidentally broaden publish rights.

title: GitHub CLI Linux package signing key expires September 5
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub warns that the Linux package signing key expires on September 5, which can break CI images or developer hosts that install gh through package managers.
actionable_takeaway: Check CI base images and developer setup scripts for gh key refresh before treating package-install failures as application failures.

title: Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot
author: GitHub Docs
why_it_matters: The supported-models page is the durable readback point for which Copilot surfaces expose each model and what constraints apply.
actionable_takeaway: Pair changelog reading with docs readback before changing team defaults or automation routing.
